Description:en: Rupture of membranes occurring less than 12 hours before delivery.
Rupture of membranes occurring between 12 and 18 hours before delivery.
Rupture of membranes occurring more than 18 hours before delivery, increasing risk of neonatal infection.
A seizure characterized by a brief lapse in consciousness accompanied by sustained muscle stiffening (tonic component).
A seizure type presenting with disturbance of memory function during the ictal period.
A seizure type presenting with disturbance of language or speech production during the ictal period.
A seizure characterized by an abnormal, sustained posturing of the body or limbs.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL ONSET SEIZURE FOLLOWED BY IMPAIRM CONSCIOUSN
Description:en: A seizure that begins with a simple partial (focal) onset and subsequently progresses to impaired consciousness.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL SEIZURE EVOLVING TO COMPLEX PARTIAL SEIZURE EVOLVING TO GENERALISED SEIZURE
Description:en: A seizure that begins focally as a simple partial seizure, evolves into a complex partial seizure, and then generalizes.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL SEIZURE WITH DISTURBANCE OF HIGHER CEREBRAL FUNCTION
Description:en: A focal seizure affecting higher cortical functions such as cognition, memory, or language, without loss of consciousness.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL SEIZURE WITH FOCAL MOTOR SIGNS WITH MARCH
Description:en: A focal motor seizure in which abnormal movements spread ("march") from one body part to adjacent areas, following the cortical motor map.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL SEIZURE WITH FOCAL MOTOR SIGNS WITHOUT MARCH
Description:en: A focal motor seizure with abnormal movement confined to one body area, without spread to adjacent areas.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL SEIZURE WITH SPECIAL SENSORY SYMPTOMS
Description:en: A focal seizure presenting with abnormal sensory phenomena (e.g. visual, auditory, olfactory, or gustatory symptoms) without loss of consciousness.

Fully specified name:en: SIMPLE PARTIAL SEIZURE, CONSCIOUSNESS NOT IMPAIRED
Description:en: A focal seizure occurring without any alteration or loss of consciousness.
A focal seizure presenting with abnormal somatosensory sensations such as tingling, numbness, or a crawling sensation.
A seizure characterized by sudden sustained increase in muscle tone (stiffening), typically lasting several seconds to a minute.
The count of convulsive (seizure) episodes observed in the newborn.
Assessment of the character of the newborn's cry (e.g. normal, hoarse, or weak) as an indicator of neurological or respiratory status.
A finding indicating that the newborn's gestational size or maturity is less than expected for a term infant.
Assessment of coldness of the newborn's skin at specific body sites, a sign of hypothermia or poor perfusion.
Assessment and grading of yellow discoloration of the newborn's skin and sclera due to elevated bilirubin.
Bluish discoloration of the central body (lips, tongue, trunk) indicating inadequate oxygenation of the blood.
Inward movement of the chest wall during inspiration, graded by severity, indicating respiratory distress.
An expiratory sound made by the newborn as a compensatory mechanism to maintain lung volume, indicating respiratory distress.
Widening of the nostrils during breathing, a sign of increased respiratory effort in the newborn.
A finding describing a diminished or feeble quality of a pulse or other clinical sign.
A finding describing an abnormally strong or forceful pulse.
The time taken for color to return to skin after pressure is applied, used to assess peripheral circulation.
A capillary refill time of less than 3 seconds, considered within the normal range.
A capillary refill time of more than 3 seconds, indicating delayed peripheral perfusion.
Diffuse edematous swelling of the fetal scalp that crosses suture lines, caused by pressure during delivery.
A congenital condition in which both nasal passages are blocked, obstructing airflow through the nose.
Assessment for physical features atypical of normal development, suggestive of a congenital syndrome.
A dysmorphic facial feature in which the bridge of the nose appears flattened.
A dysmorphic facial feature consisting of a skin fold of the upper eyelid covering the inner corner of the eye.
Examination findings related to abnormalities of the external genitalia or anus.
A congenital defect in which the anal opening is absent or blocked, preventing normal passage of stool.
A congenital limb abnormality in which one or both radius bones of the forearm are missing.
A midline skin lesion combining a birthmark (naevus) and a fatty lump (lipoma), often associated with underlying spinal defects.
A deep dimple or indentation over the sacral region, which may indicate an underlying spinal abnormality.
Intravenous delivery of complete nutritional support, used when a newborn cannot be fed enterally.
A feeding schedule in which the newborn is fed at 2-hour intervals.
A feeding schedule in which the newborn is fed at 3-hour intervals.

Fully specified name:en: POTASSIUM CHLORIDE 40 MMOL/SODIUM CHLORIDE 0.9% INFUSION SOLUTION
Description:en: An intravenous infusion combining potassium chloride 40 mmol with 0.9% sodium chloride, used for electrolyte replacement.
Indicates whether the newborn was placed in an incubator or otherwise kept warm to maintain thermoregulation.
